question: Who wrote the Summa Theologiae, and when did he live?

teaching.title: Thomas Aquinas and the Summa Theologiae
teaching.body: St. Thomas Aquinas (1225-1274), a Dominican friar, wrote the Summa Theologiae (Summary of Theology) as a systematic synthesis of Christian theology and Aristotelian philosophy. Left unfinished at his death, it covers God's existence and nature, creation, ethics, the Incarnation, and the sacraments. Aquinas's method — presenting objections, then replies — became the model for scholastic theology. Pope Leo XIII's encyclical Aeterni Patris (1879) recommended Thomism as the standard for Catholic philosophical and theological education.
